Anonymous usage statistics use Microsoft Clarity. On by default; it is turned off if you skip the onboarding before reaching the usage statistics step, and you can change it in Settings. When on, Clarity still collects metadata such as device model, OS version, IP address, and tap coordinates. Strict masking is enabled in Clarity, so on-screen text and input (including server addresses, keys, console content, and player info) is masked. Checking for updates contacts the GitHub API. Nothing else is uploaded; server data is only sent to your own server.
The Lora and Poppins fonts in the interface are provided under the SIL Open Font License.

Monitoring, management, operations, and app settings are grouped here; bottom bar features are also reachable from here.
First tab. See whether the server is online, how far the round has progressed, and how many people are on.
Second tab. Search online players, and kick, ban, or message them.
Third tab. Send commands straight to the server; the output stays below.
Fourth tab. Draws the facility on your phone from this round\'s seed and marks player locations.
Last tab. Adapted plugins, files, voice, and bans are all here. Liquid Glass can be turned on in Settings.
Enter the host address and VerifyToken first
The fingerprint must be a 32-byte SHA-256; colons or spaces are allowed
A mobile client for viewing and managing SCP:SL servers. It connects directly to SLDataAPI on your server; addresses and keys are stored only on this phone.
When on, you need to unlock with fingerprint, face, or screen lock when starting the app or returning after more than 30 seconds. Off by default; you can change it in Settings later.
You can leave this step empty. If both host and VerifyToken are filled in, tapping Next saves it and makes it the current server.
verify_token reads monitoring data and is set in the plugin\'s config.yml. The API Key runs control actions, is used from SLDataAPI 2.6 on, and is created in the game console:

A key\'s permissions are fixed when it\'s created. For a duty key, replace the trailing admin with duty when creating it. If you later need admin permission, create another admin key in-game and switch to it in the app. You can leave the key empty and only view monitoring. When the plugin supports TLS the connection is encrypted; this requires an SLDataAPI build with TLS.
You can paste it in advance. If left empty, you\'ll confirm it against the console when testing the encrypted connection.
The bottom bar has five tabs. The Hub also leads to adapted plugins and settings.

Anonymous usage statistics (Microsoft Clarity) show which screens are hard to use so the app can keep improving. When on, Clarity still collects metadata such as device model, OS version, IP address, and tap coordinates. Strict masking is enabled in Clarity, so on-screen text and input (including server addresses, keys, console content, and player info) is masked.

If you tap \"Skip\" before reaching this step, usage statistics stay off. If you skip or continue from this step without choosing, they\'re on by default. You can change this in Settings later. Apart from that, the app only contacts GitHub when checking for updates; server data only travels between your phone and your own server.

Credentials are stored only on this phone (encrypted with AndroidKeyStore) and only sent to your own server, never through any third party. When the plugin supports TLS, HTTPS/WSS is used and the server\'s self-signed certificate is pinned. On first connection, compare the console fingerprint (sldataapi cert show, or the TLS banner at startup) before trusting it. Requires an SLDataAPI build with TLS; old versions or tls_mode off show \"This connection is not encrypted\".

After resetting, the app will allow plaintext again if the encrypted handshake fails. Only do this if you\'re sure this server has turned TLS off. Plaintext connections always show \"This connection is not encrypted\".

Adds frosted blur and highlights to navigation and cards.\nTurning it off restores solid colors and persists after restart.
On Android 12 and later, content scrolling behind is blurred in real time; older versions use translucency instead. Text stays readable.
On launch, queries the GitHub API (api.github.com) for new versions, at most once every 6 hours. Only public release info is read; no server info or personal data is sent.

Uses Microsoft Clarity to record how the interface is used, to improve the app. Clarity still collects metadata such as device model, OS version, IP address, and tap coordinates. Strict masking is enabled in Clarity, so on-screen text and input (including server addresses, keys, input fields, console content, and player info) is masked. Turning it off stops collection immediately and it won\'t resume next time. On first launch, if you skip onboarding before reaching the usage statistics step, this stays off.
When on, you need to unlock with fingerprint, face, or screen lock when starting the app or returning after more than 30 seconds.
